{"source_id":"MS002-SRC-A","verdicts":[
{"claim_id":"CL-0201","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0335 and EV-0336 show the loop asking for batch size, copy pool, output location/delivery and old batches, with the speaker answering manually.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0335","EV-0336"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0202","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0337 states the need for more autonomy since the operator is not around, and EV-0338/EV-0339 describe passing prior generated ads through itself each run and making something new and time-based that varies day to day.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0337","EV-0338","EV-0339"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0203","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0339 says it has done a little testing and will do a real batch render to show how it works before instituting it on the computer via cron.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0339"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0204","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0340 states it first checks a scheduling skill because Claude ('cloud') has a built-in skill called schedule that outlines how to do this.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0340"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0205","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0341 explicitly says 'We went from prompts to skills, skills to loops, and now we need to go from loops to routines.'","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0341"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0206","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0341-EV-0343 state the loop still runs on the speaker's computer requiring an office machine someone signs into daily, versus a cloud-based version running autonomously on a schedule dumping output into a company-accessible folder.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0341","EV-0342","EV-0343"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0207","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0344 and EV-0345 contain the prompt stating the completed prompt-to-skill and skill-to-loop steps, generating into a shareable Google Drive folder for team members, and asking to be walked through step by step and set it up, noting platform access will be needed.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0344","EV-0345"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0208","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0346 quotes the model proposing to kill the local one and turn it into something on the internet while asking 'does that sound okay with you?'","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0346"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0209","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0346 mentions the time zone, EV-0347 the GitHub repo creation and routine one-time setup information, and EV-0348 the Google Drive information and private GitHub repo.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0346","EV-0347","EV-0348"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0210","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0347 defines a GitHub repo as 'an online place to put code so that code can run without my involvement.'","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0347"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0211","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0350-EV-0352 describe opening cloud.ai/customize connectors, going to settings and connectors at the bottom, connecting and authorizing in a browser with the Google account, then returning and saying 'connected'.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0350","EV-0351","EV-0352"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0212","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0353 says the connector can't change sharing settings, so the speaker goes to share and sets 'anyone with the link can now view', then returns and says 'good to go'.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0352","EV-0353"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0213","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0354 and EV-0355 state Google Drive was already connected locally but now needs to be connected in the cloud routine instead, after which the routine is created.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0354","EV-0355"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0214","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0355 mentions the test run and routines in the top left-hand corner, and EV-0356 shows the routine listed and 'testing it right now which is why the status is still paused'.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0355","EV-0356"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0215","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0356 gives the task and EV-0357 gives the context describing the repo plus 'cloud code remote Google Drive as connectors' and the GitHub repository.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0356","EV-0357"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0216","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0358 and EV-0359 state that whenever you see the cloud logo the work is not occurring on your computer, which means it doesn't depend on you.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0358","EV-0359"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0217","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0359 and EV-0360 describe verifying the output directory contents before uploading, creating a dated subfolder in Google Drive, and uploading the ads.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0359","EV-0360"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0218","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0302 shows keeping it simple with just linear rather than radial bursts, and EV-0303 states 'they tend to use inter for everything' and wanting his to look different/stand out, with EV-0304 selecting Red Hat display.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0301","EV-0302","EV-0303","EV-0304"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0219","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0305 and EV-0306 show making everything bigger, zooming out, the remark that one of the biggest problems with ads is people can't see them, and people looking at it on their phones.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0305","EV-0306"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0220","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0321 and EV-0322 describe selecting liked ads, downloading them onto the computer, and them being straightforward to upload to Google/Facebook ads or whatever ad library manager is used.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0321","EV-0322"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0221","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0364 states Claude doesn't have image or video generation built in, and EV-0365/EV-0366 say Claude generated assets by driving compositing tools like Photoshop, Canva, or Microsoft Paint equivalents.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0364","EV-0365","EV-0366"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0222","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0366 says Claude baked in a set of instructions and EV-0367 says it steered these until outputs were produced, hardcoding every pixel, headline and text on the page.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0366","EV-0367"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0223","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0368 states 'we can't really extend far past that' and that procedurally generated outputs 'are just not always going to be of the best quality.'","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0368"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0224","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0369 describes version two where instead of Claude generating assets, direct image and video models are steered by Claude just like Photoshop, Canva and Microsoft Paint were steered.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0369","EV-0370"]},
{"claim_id":"CL-0225","judgment":"ENTAILED","entail_why":"EV-0370 says Photoshop composites a bunch of different elements and EV-0371 says you control them while GPT Image 2 produces the pixels directly, turning text into an array of pixels.","evidence_refs_checked":["EV-0370","EV-0371"]}
]}
